Why:
- Market size and spend: iOS App Store consumer revenue is vastly larger than the Mac App Store, with higher daily engagement and conversion.
- Purchasing friction: Mobile users are more inclined to impulse buys and recurring subscriptions.
- Discovery: iOS benefits from far greater organic search, editorial exposure, and ad reach.

When macOS can outperform:
- High-value pro/dev/creative tools, menu bar utilities, and B2B apps can command higher prices with lower volume.
- Direct sales or enterprise licensing (often outside the Mac App Store) can outperform if you have a defined niche and distribution channel.

Why for an iOS-first revenue focus:
- Deep access to latest iOS APIs (App Intents, Live Activities, Widgets, SwiftData) without bridges.
- Best native performance, UI fidelity, and smaller app size.
- Faster alignment with new iOS releases; fewer dependency and SDK lag risks.
- Simpler ops: one codebase, no native-module glue or JS runtime concerns.
- Easier App Store compliance than OTA patching workflows common in RN.

Choose React Native if:
- Day-1 Android parity is mandatory or near-term.
- Team is primarily JS/TS and you can absorb native-module work for iOS-specific features.
- You need shared UI/business logic across mobile (and possibly web via RN Web).

Clarifier: Do you need Android in v1 or within the next 1–2 quarters? If yes, RN may be justified; if iOS-only for the foreseeable future, SwiftUI is the pragmatic choice.
